messages:
Maya (PM): quick thread — we shipped the baseline last week, customers are starting to surface follow-on asks. can we agree on a simple bug vs enhancement rubric and a short list for next sprint? link: https://redwood/repo/roadmap#next-wave :eyes:
Sam - Eng: +1. can we keep it to 3 slots (1 engineering, 2 small/med) to avoid scope creep?
Alex P: I vote for 1 high-impact bug fix, 1 UX polish, 1 perf tweak. we should factor in customer escalations.
Kevin (Support): FYI we have 4 customers with the same autocomplete mismatch report (error rate ~3%) — one is on a paid SLA. labeling that as "customer-impact" in our board.
Diana QA: repro steps here: `POST /generate` with prompt "..." then token shift at n=12. failing in chrome and firefox. I can attach logs.
Maya (PM): thanks — sounds like a bug candidate. proposal: anything causing incorrect outputs or data loss = bug (fix in next hotfix cycle). everything else = enhancement (add to grooming). acceptance criteria for bugs: clear repro, regression test, canary validation, <2% error after fix.
Sam - Eng: practical ask — what's our threshold for pulling an enhancement into the hotfix sprint? cost vs signal?
Maya (PM): rule of thumb: if customer SLA or revenue risk, we treat as bug. else enhancement. also consider frequency x severity > threshold (we'll use a simple score).
Alex P: propose score = (#customers reporting * severity_weight) + (support_tickets_last_7d). severity_weight: critical=10, major=5, minor=1. if score>=15 -> escalate.
Nora-bot: automated note: created triage board column "next-wave-prioritize" and copied flagged tickets.
Kevin (Support): applying Alex's scoring now to the four autocomplete cases — score = 4*5 + 3 = 23 -> escalated.
Diana QA: can we add a quick checklist for triage in the ticket? I'm thinking: reproduction steps, affected versions, sample input/output, first_seen_ts, regression_test (y/n).
Maya (PM): agreed. I'll add that template to the ticket. also asking eng: can we estimate the autocomplete fix? rough ballpark ok.
Sam - Eng: rough estimate: 2 dev days + 1 QA day + canary rollout -> schedule for next sprint if prioritized. risk: it touches tokenizer mapping so need careful tests.
Alex P: other candidate: UI reorder of settings — low risk, 3 dev days, maybe defer to sprint+1.
Maya (PM): shortlist for next sprint: (1) autocomplete correctness (bug, SLA customer), (2) low-latency decoder fallback (enhancement, perf, medium), (3) settings reorder (enhancement, low). we keep a parking lot for small UX tweaks.
Sam - Eng: +1 to that slate. will create PRD-lite bullets and link to this thread.
Diana QA: I'll put together regression tests for autocomplete and add to CI as a gating check.
Kevin (Support): I'll draft customer comms for impacted customers and include expected timeline.
Maya (PM): launch criteria for the fix: reproduction + unit/regression tests in CI, canary with 10% traffic for 48h with <1% error, rollback plan documented. once met, we bump patch.
Alex P: one more ask — can we track post-fix customer satisfaction (NPS-ish) at 2 weeks? helps validate impact.
Maya (PM): good call. adding metric: affected-customer-sat (pre/post).
Nora-bot: reminder scheduled: weekly triage sync every Tue 10:00am.
Sam - Eng: I'll post a short RFC with the tokenizer change and link backlog items.
Maya (PM): perfect — thanks team. I'll update the roadmap board and move items into "sprint-next". ping me if you need re-prioritization before EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
